Your account and device data live only in your own Firebase project. Being paired never means permanent access — every session asks again.

Family Remote Support helps trusted people help each other with phones. This policy explains exactly what data the app uses.

What is collected
• Your account: name, email and Google account id you sign in with.
• Your device: model, manufacturer, Android version and app version.
• A random, app-scoped device id so your phones can be listed.
• Push token: used only to tell your phone that someone asked to help you.
• Session records: who asked whom, start/end time and the final status. This is the honest activity history you see in the app.

What is NEVER collected
• Screen content. Live screen video exists only during a session you approved; it is streamed directly between the two phones and is not stored.
• Passwords, screen text, key strokes or photos.
• Location. The Live location tab is a placeholder — nothing is collected today.

Where your data lives
Only in the Firebase project that belongs to this app. It is not sold, not shared with advertisers, and not used for tracking.

Who can see what
A paired helper can see your device's online status and can open a session only after you explicitly approve each request. You can revoke a paired phone at any time, and signing out deletes this phone's presence and push token.

You stay in control: every session needs your live approval, shows a clear indicator while it runs, and can be stopped by you at any moment.

These rules keep Family Remote Support safe for everyone.

1. Consent first. Every single help session needs a fresh, explicit approval on the phone that receives help. Pairing alone never grants access.

2. Pairing codes are one-time and expire in about 5 minutes. A code can be redeemed only once and only by the person who scans or types it in time.

3. Guest help is temporary. A guest connection expires by itself after 2 hours and can never become a permanent family pairing by itself.

4. You can always stop. The person being helped can deny a request, end a running session at any second, or revoke a paired phone completely.

5. The helper must be trusted. Only share your code or QR with people you actually trust. A helper sees your screen while a session runs — close sensitive apps first if you are unsure.

6. No bypassing. The app never tries to unlock a phone, read passwords, silently grant permissions, or hide that a session is running. It only works inside what Android explicitly allows.

7. Fair use only. Do not use the app to harass, spy on, or pressure anyone. Abuse leads to revoked access.

8. Families first. This app is built for helping family members and close friends with their phones — nothing else.

How to turn on Remote assist
Follow the 3 steps below exactly — you only ever need to do this once:
In Settings, find the \"Family Remote Support assist\" row in the list (our app\'s row — it is usually highlighted).
Tap the row and turn the switch ON.
When the Android warning appears, tap Allow.
⚠️ Careful: turning on \"Accessibility menu shortcut\" or any other switch will not work — that one is not ours! Only the \"Family Remote Support assist\" row is correct.

There are two kinds of links. FAMILY code = a permanent trusted phone — once linked, no code is needed again. GUEST code = a 2-hour temporary link (for an outside helper) — it removes itself when time is up, and a Guest never becomes Family automatically. Being linked is not permission — every session needs separate live approval on the recipient\'s phone, and the session ends by itself after a set time.

If it still fails, publish the newest android-app/firestore.rules from the repo (Firebase console → Firestore Database → Rules).
